S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient_info.stressor: When the Bronx distribution center merged two inventory teams, Brian was abruptly made acting workflow lead because of his skill with SAP WM, Excel analytics, and layout redesign, even though he had always preferred quiet technical work over supervising people. At first he tried to absorb the added meetings, conflict between pickers, and pressure to justify every efficiency metric by retreating into longer spreadsheets and late-night Python fixes. Over the next 4 months, his stress-related response began interfering with his accuracy, his recreational basketball attendance, and his solitary art routines, making the change clinically significant rather than just unpleasant. After a performance check-in noted missed cycle-count deadlines and visible strain, Brian accepted an Employee Assistance Program referral and scheduled a psychiatric evaluation.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: I’m here because ever since they made me the acting workflow lead, I’ve been walking into the warehouse already tense, snapping over little SAP errors, missing cycle-count deadlines I never used to miss, and then going home too drained to play basketball or even work on my sketches.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Symptoms must develop within 3 months of the onset of the stressor
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: The lead role started after the team merger, and within the first month or two I could tell I wasn’t handling work the way I normally do.

additional_requirement_2.name: Additional Requirement 2
additional_requirement_2.description: Within 6 months of the termination of the stressor or its consequences
additional_requirement_2.manifestation: The acting lead responsibilities are still in place, so this hasn’t continued on after the work change ended; I’m still dealing with the change every day.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My supervisor had to bring up missed cycle-count deadlines in a performance check-in, and I’ve stopped showing up for basketball and my usual sketching time because work is taking over my life.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about four months, since they merged the inventory teams and put me in the acting workflow lead role.
